Yes
From the backend developer seat, the trial demonstrated that the real-shape corpus with encodings and fix neighbours is workable, unambiguous, and fair. The blocking findings metric stayed at or below target across all three cards (2, 0, and 1), and neither card 430 nor 422 encountered blocking findings due to gaps in corpus families or encodings. Slice times remained manageable and close to the 20-minute threshold without needing to game the rules or cut corners on red-green-refactor cycles. Separating caller and CI-shape rows into Decider D270 keeps this practice focused and directly actionable during card execution.
